title: ExhaustRecord
description: Metaphor→Mechanism W6.1 (design-register: exhaust-accounting). The ledger of what a compute DISCARDED — the thermodynamic exhaust of the intake→compression cycle. Every governed compute or compaction may emit one; the sealing receipt carries exhaust_sha = sha256 of this record's canonical JSON, binding the discard ledger to the proof spine without inlining content (items carry hashes and sizes, never payloads — exhaust must not become a data-exfiltration channel). INVARIANT EX-I1: an ExhaustRecord is append-only evidence; it never alters the compute's outputs. INVARIANT EX-I2: items reference content by sha256 only. The record exists so the exhaust→intake loop is possible at all: a consolidation job can mine discarded-but-later-needed items to tune retrieval and spaced repetition, which is the design's core idea — learning from what was thrown away.

source.description: Which mechanism produced the exhaust: a governed compute (gateway), context compaction (agent-machine), a retrieval stage that fetched-then-dropped, or a deliberation loop that rejected candidates.

counts.description: How much was discarded, by kind. All fields optional; absent means zero/not-tracked.

bytesIn.description: Canonical-serialized size of what entered the stage. bytesOut/bytesIn is the v1 entropy proxy (compression ratio).

bytesOut.description: Canonical-serialized size of what left the stage.

items.description: The discarded items, by reference only (EX-I2).
